questions.questionText: Which of the following is not true in the case of second theorem of welfare economics?
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following is not true in the case of second theorem of welfare economics?
options: If consumers exhibit convex preferences, every pareto efficient allocation is a possible competitive equilibrium in a pure exchange economy.
In an economy involving production, the convexity of production sets ensures that a pareto efficient allocation can be achieved as a market equilibrium.
It holds when there are increasing returns to scale.
It implies that in the market system, the allocation role and the distributive role can be separated from each other. UGC NTA
optionsEn: If consumers exhibit convex preferences, every pareto efficient allocation is a possible competitive equilibrium in a pure exchange economy.
In an economy involving production, the convexity of production sets ensures that a pareto efficient allocation can be achieved as a market equilibrium.
It holds when there are increasing returns to scale.
It implies that in the market system, the allocation role and the distributive role can be separated from each other. UGC NTA
questions.explanation: Welfare economics is associated with two major theorems. First, that competitive markets produce Pareto optimal outcomes and second, that social welfare can be maximized at equilibrium with an appropriate level of redistribution. In the case of second theorem, if consumers exhibit perfect choice, then every Pareto efficient allocation is a possible competitive equilibrium in a pure exchange economy. In a production economy the convexity of the production set ensures that a Pareto efficient allocation is a possible competitive equilibrium in a pure exchange economy. In a production economy the convexity of the production set ensures that a Pareto efficient allocation can be achieved as a market equilibrium. This means that in the market system the allocative role and the distribution role can be mutually separated. Hence, option (c) is not correct.
questions.explanationEn: Welfare economics is associated with two major theorems. First, that competitive markets produce Pareto optimal outcomes and second, that social welfare can be maximized at equilibrium with an appropriate level of redistribution. In a production economy the convexity of the production set ensures that a Pareto efficient allocation is a possible competitive equilibrium in a pure exchange economy. In a production economy the convexity of the production set ensures that a Pareto efficient allocation can be achieved as a market equilibrium. This means that in the market system the allocative role and the distribution role can be mutually separated. Hence, option (c) is not correct.

questions.questionText: The voluntary exchange theory of public finance was given by:
questions.questionTextEn: The voluntary exchange theory of public finance was given by:
questions.explanation: Voluntary exchange theory of public finance was given by Eric Lindahl. Under the voluntary exchange theory, tax levels are set automatically, as taxpayers pay in proportion to the government benefits they receive. To put is another way, those who benefit most from public goods pay the most taxes.

questions.explanation: This law was propounded by Wiseman and peacock that public expenditure increases in jerks and in steps and not in a continuous manner. Peacock Wiseman analysis is based on the political theory of public expenditure determination. Wiseman and Peacock studies the changes in public expenditure in Britain over the period 1890-1955.
